title: Sunway D'Hill: forest views with city convenience.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #459 | SUNWAY D'HILL, KOTA DAMANSARA
excerpt: A completed mixed development backing onto a forest reserve, where the arrival sequence, the car park and the landscape deck all show a developer refining the same playbook.
takeaways: Two towers beside a forest reserve, with every unit facing the hill.
Separate shop and residential entrances, and the densest landscaped deck Sean has seen.
A four-lane road, a busy retail podium and nearby new supply are the concerns.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Sunway D'Hill is a two-tower mixed development of 976 homes next to a forest reserve, with every unit facing the hill. Shoppers use a front entrance and residents a separate one at the back, and all 29 shops are held and leased by the developer. A weatherproof drop-off, speed ramps to six car park levels and a step-free route lead home.

The facility deck is the most densely landscaped Sean has seen, with an infinity lap pool, elevated walkways, sunken courts and a glass gym. The 1,238 sq ft, four-bedroom Type D, with a glass-walled wet kitchen, was RM850,000, about RM700 psf, on leasehold commercial land.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: It is on Persiaran Mahogany, the quieter, residential side of Kota Damansara lined with bungalows and schools, one road from Persiaran Surian's Thomson Hospital, SRI KDU, malls, MRT and the DASH highway. Kwasa Damansara is across the street.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Sean calls D'Hill a project designed for own stay, and says he wouldn't mind living there himself. With other completed projects nearby, he puts three-bedroom rents at about RM3 psf, which he says makes sense at this price.

pros: A developer that keeps improving: separate commercial and residential entrances, a covered, naturally ventilated drop-off that feels like a convention centre, and a private lobby for each tower.
The landscape and details: winding paths on several levels, sunken courts next to visitor parking, two speed ramps, step-free access, magnetic fire doors and every unit framing the hill.
A balance of town and nature on a tight budget: the calm of Persiaran Mahogany, with the hospital, MRT, university, industry and DASH one road away.
cons: The micro site: Persiaran Mahogany is a four-lane road, so engines will be loud against the quiet, and social housing and old apartments surround the site.
The mixed development: the shops are almost fully let and are the nearest groceries, so the podium may get crowded, though developer management and a back service lane help.
Competition: five or six new projects across the road in Kwasa Damansara. D'Hill's edge is that it is finished, with three-bedroom rents of around RM3 psf.

closing: Among the hillside projects Sean has seen lately, this one stands out at its price, especially for buyers who want to move in now.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this July 2026 episode. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. The developer let Sean view the completed project.
